title: Time bound for a singleton output
statement: Let $C$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet with at least one work tape, and let $\mathrm{entry}$ and $\mathrm{exit}$ be states of $C$. Let $x$ be a Boolean word, $b$ a Boolean value, and $t>0$. Suppose that the run of $C$ from the canonical entry configuration carrying $x$ on tape zero is not in state $\mathrm{exit}$ at any time $j$ with $0<j<t$, and at time $t$ reaches the canonical exit configuration carrying the singleton word $[b]$ on tape zero. Then the wrapper computes $[b]$ from input $x$ within $2\operatorname{length}(x)+2+t+1$ steps.
hypotheses_covered: $C$ is a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
$C$ has at least one work tape
entry and exit are states of $C$
At each integer time $j$ with $0<j<t$, the run from the canonical entry configuration is not in state exit
At time $t$, the run from the canonical entry configuration equals the canonical exit configuration carrying $[b]$ on tape zero
replaced:
Suppose the inner machine, started in its entry state at the seam carrying $x$,
first returns to the exit state at a positive time $t$ with the singleton word
$[b]$ on tape zero. Then the decider wrapper computes the output $[b]$ from
input $x$ within $2|x| + 2 + t + 1$ steps, with no earlier emission.
